digest.description: Content digest when the resolver can supply one.

Assertion.description:
A concept asserted in a category during processing, with confidence level and provenance metadata.

Assertions are the core data unit flowing through the engine pipeline. `confidence` records how the assertion was produced: `'certain'` when read or handed in as stated, `'inferred'` when an inference rule added it, and `'repaired'` when the engine added or rewrote it while repairing the marking. The engine does not assign `'uncertain'` itself. `source` says where the assertion came from. `expiresAt` records caller-supplied expiry metadata. The engine does not evaluate that date or automatically change confidence or the marking; the host applies its expiry policy.

categoryId.description: The id of the category the concept is asserted in.

confidence.description: How the assertion was produced: `certain` when read or handed in as stated, `inferred` when an inference rule added it, or `repaired` when the engine added or rewrote it while repairing the marking. The engine does not assign `uncertain` itself.

expiresAt.description: Caller-supplied ISO 8601 expiry date; the engine does not evaluate it.

metadata.description: Caller-defined data attached to the assertion. The engine assigns it no meaning.

provenance.description:
Source provenance for the concept that backed this assertion.

Populated only when the concept came from an external source whose records were loaded with the scheme (typically one a scheme's `concepts.external` block declares). Inline-backed assertions leave this field undefined to keep payloads compact for the common single-source case. A concept a scheme document declares in its `inline` list has none, even when one of that document's `external` sources also serves a record with its id. A concept read through a queryable-only source (`SourceCapabilities.queryableOnly`) has none either: that source is asked per lookup and never loaded whole, and a lookup does not say which source answered. Such a source still appears in a composed operation's `resolution.sources`. Across a layered stack the later layer decides: a concept a later layer's source supplies carries that source's provenance even when an earlier document declares it inline, and a concept a later layer declares inline carries none.

Identity fields mirror the source's `sourceIdentity()` observation at engine-load time (or the immutable value the Context pinned).

replacedConceptId.description:
The deprecated concept this assertion was modernized from.

Set when processing rewrote a deprecated concept into the replacement its scheme declares. `conceptId` is the current concept every downstream stage evaluates; this field records what the data was actually marked with, so an explanation can show the substitution ("concept A was replaced by concept B; B is what your access was compared against") instead of silently presenting a concept the document never carried.

It travels on the assertion rather than alongside it because assertion arrays are the engine's state transport: an access check made from transported assertions can still explain the substitution.

source.description:
Where this assertion came from. An open string: the engine labels the facts it adds, and a caller or a host may label the facts it hands in however it likes.

Four labels mean the engine derived the fact, so it derives the fact again each time it settles a marking: `infer`, and `repair` with a `sourceRule`, a fact a scheme rule adds; `default`, a category's default concept; and `context`, a value a part took from its whole. When validate, process or explain settles a marking, a fact handed in under one of them is set aside and comes back only if the engine derives it again, so no label can make a removal silent.

Every other label is the author's statement and is kept as given: `parse` (read from text), `user` (handed in by a caller), `aggregate` (a value a rollup states as its own, even one a contributor derived or took from its whole), every other label the engine writes on a result, and any label a caller or host chooses, such as `stated`.

sourceRule.description: The id of the scheme rule that produced this assertion, when one did. Otherwise an engine-owned id beginning with `_`, set when the scheme's structure, not a rule, added the assertion. The engine writes two: `_tier_child_requires_parent` (a tier parent required by a stated child) and `_header_of_stated_member` (a header filled in for a stated member). A scheme rule id never begins with `_`.

value.description:
The value of a concept that takes one (`text_input`).

A value handed in is read the way a value in text is: it settles in the spelling the concept's encoding stores. One the encoding cannot read is reported as the error `_invalid_assertion_value`, and a concept that takes a value, handed in with none, as `_missing_assertion_value`. See `ValidationError`.

AssertionConfidence.description: Confidence assigned to an assertion by the processing pipeline.

Attribution.description:
Provenance attached to every source so downstream consumers can render proper attribution and license notices.

Mandatory because most source data we'll integrate (NIST, ICS, IANA, external taxonomies) requires citation. Sources that don't have a formal license should set `license: 'unspecified'` rather than omit it.

citation.description: Suggested citation string for academic / regulatory use.

license.description: SPDX identifier or short license token (e.g. "CC-BY-4.0", "public-domain").

licenseUrl.description: Canonical URL where the license terms can be inspected.

name.description: Display name of the upstream source (e.g. "NIST CSWP-29").

ContextAccessRef.description:
The access-policy reference in a Context. An access ref carries the policy's `id` + `version` and optionally a list of layer refs that stack on top of the base. Layers belong inside the access entry because a layer is semantically a derivative of _that_ policy; it cannot be paired with a different base, so nesting it under the policy keeps that coupling explicit.

An access layer only ever adds. See `AccessLayer` for why overriding or removing an inherited mapping is a composition error rather than a merge.

layers.description: Optional layer references applied left-to-right after the base access policy.

version.description: A concrete semver version, or `latest` for the highest published one.

ContextCrosswalkRef.description: A crosswalk reference in a Context. A crosswalk ref carries the crosswalk's `id` + `version` and optionally a list of layer refs that stack on top of the base. Layers belong inside the crosswalk entry because a layer is semantically a derivative of _that_ crosswalk; it cannot be paired with a different base, so nesting it under the crosswalk keeps that coupling explicit.

layers.description: Optional layer references applied left-to-right after the base crosswalk.

version.description: A concrete semver version, or `latest` for the highest published one.

ContextGuideRef.description:
A guide reference in a Context. A guide ref carries the guide's `id` + `version` and optionally a list of layer refs that stack on top of the base. Layers belong inside the guide entry because a layer is semantically a derivative of _that_ guide; it cannot be paired with a different base, so nesting it under the guide keeps that coupling explicit.

Adding guidance needs no layer, since a Context holds a list of guides. Layering is for tailoring a guide the composing organization received read-only.

layers.description: Optional layer references applied left-to-right after the base guide.

version.description: A concrete semver version, or `latest` for the highest published one.

ContextSchemeRef.description: The scheme reference in a Context. A scheme ref carries the scheme's `id` + `version` and optionally a list of layer refs that stack on top of the base. Layers belong inside the scheme block because a layer is semantically a derivative of _that_ scheme; it cannot be paired with a different base, so nesting it under the scheme keeps that coupling explicit.

layers.description: Optional layer references applied left-to-right after the base scheme.

version.description: A concrete semver version, or `latest` for the highest published one.

ProcessingContext.description: Caller-supplied context describing the role of a marking being processed. No context (or role='whole') means an overall/document-level marking. role='part' means a portion/paragraph that belongs to another marking.

partOf.description:
The whole marking this is part of (when role='part').

The whole does two jobs. In a role-aware scheme it is the reading context for the scheme's whole-aware rules: a rule condition with `target: 'context'` is answered from it. And in every scheme, role-aware or not, `process`, `validate` and `explain` compare a part that is valid on its own with its whole. That is the comparison a whole is judged by against its parts and the one `checkCoverage` gives, asked of this one part: category by category, in the direction each category's rollup declares. A category a rollup pipeline resolves is judged instead by what rolling the whole up with this part would add or drop. A category whose rollup has no direction one part can be judged by, such as `first`, is left to the whole.

What the part carries beyond its whole is one `_exceeds_whole` error on the part. Its `affectedConcepts` names every finding: first what the whole does not cover, then what the whole carries that the part does not allow. Its `categoryId` is set when every finding is in one category. It offers no fix, because whether the part or the whole should change is the author's call. A part that breaks its own rules reports those errors and is not compared. Its own rules are the scheme's: an in-process engine's `afterValidate` plugin runs after the comparison and does not change whether it happens. A call's `parts` and a document scan or audit read each part in the whole without this comparison; they judge coverage on the whole instead.

A part is compared with its whole as the engine settles the whole: read, modernized, completed by what the scheme's rules imply and judged, the same settling `valid` reports for the whole on its own. A whole spelled with a retired concept is compared as its replacement, and a fact the whole's rules add is one the part is compared with.

The same holds wherever a part meets its whole: here; for each of a call's `parts`, however the call's whole came, as text or as facts; and for each input `SchemeEngineAdapter.aggregate` reads against a whole. A part that takes a value from its whole, such as a list it stands for, takes it from that settled whole.

What the part gets depends on the state of its whole:

- A whole that reads and is valid is verified. The part's rules read it, and `process`, `validate` and `explain` compare the part with it.
- A whole that reads but is invalid, or does not read, is not verified. The part is still read and judged by its own rules but is not compared with the whole, so it never carries `_exceeds_whole`. It always carries the `_whole_unverified` notice.
- With no whole given, the part is judged by its own rules alone. It carries the `_whole_unverified` notice only when one of its rules was left unresolved.

Without a verified whole, what needs the whole is left open instead of guessed: a rule condition with `target: 'context'` is unresolved, so its rule never fires, as `RuleConditionTarget` describes.

TestAssertion.description: One expected result at an exact JSON path. Array indices are decimal path segments. Equality compares the complete value; contains and excludes check string substrings, object fields, or an array item matching the expected value's fields. Exists and absent test presence, including values that are false or null, and omit value.

TestCase.description: One portable input and its separately authored oracle.

assertions.description: Every assertion must match for the case to pass.

description.description: What the case checks and why.

id.description: Case id, unique across the suite and its parents.

operation.description: The Context operation the case runs.

options.description: Operation-native options, with unknown keys refused by the runner.

TestComposition.description: Exact artifact composition; suite validation refuses mutable versions.

crosswalks.description: The crosswalks the cases run with, each at an exact version.

guides.description: The guides the cases run with, each at an exact version.

scheme.description: The scheme the cases run against, at an exact version, with any layers.

TestInput.description: Typed, inert operation inputs; boundary validation enforces each operation's key set.

assertions.description: The facts an operation reads instead of marking text, or that `render` and `suggestForCategories` start from.

categoryIds.description: The categories a `suggestForCategories` case asks options for.

context.description: Request context values a `checkAccess` case passes to the access policy.

guideDeterminations.description: Analyst decisions on guide nominations, for a document case.

guideId.description: The guide a `guideScan` or `guideEvaluate` case uses. A scan with none covers every loaded guide.

marking.description: The marking text a single-marking operation reads.

markings.description: The markings an `aggregate` case rolls up.

responseProfile.description: How much a document case's result carries.

ruleIds.description: The guide rules a `guideEvaluate` case selects.

text.description: The text a scan or document operation reads.

translation.description: The translation request for a `translate` case.

userAttributes.description: The user's attributes for a `checkAccess` case.

TestOperation.description:
Canonical Context operations available to a portable test case.

`valid` and `inputWasValid` mean the same under `validate` and `process`, so a case that asserts them reads the same under either: no option changes how a marking is settled (see `TestOptions`). `rendered` reads the same under both too: a case that names no `outputFormat` gets the default for the marking's role, by the one rule `RenderConfigDoc.surfaces` states. A process case adds the authoring fields to assert on, and an `explain` case asserts on the trace, which only explain returns.

TestOptions.description:
Inert native operation options; executable callbacks and adapters cannot enter a suite.

None of them changes how a marking is settled, so there is no option to settle less than the engine does. Whether text was right as written is what `inputWasValid` and `appliedFixes` answer, and reading is tolerant on purpose.

confidence.description: Whether a `guideScan` case adds advisory confidence to each span.

context.description: The role the input is read in and the whole it belongs to.

filter.description: The text a `suggest` case filters concepts by.

includeGated.description: Whether a `suggest` case also lists concepts the filter matches but the scheme's rules currently gate.

inputFormat.description: The format the input is written in. Omitted, recognition works it out.

outputFormat.description: The format the result is written in.

outputs.description: The outputs a process case writes into `renders`, by output address.

parts.description: Part markings the whole must cover, for a validate, process or explain case. The whole is judged as covering them.

preservation.description: What a `render` case asks for: `projection`, the ordinary human projection, or `full`, which fails rather than leave any part of the state unwritten.

suggestFor.description: The categories a process case asks picker options for.

surface.description: The validation surface the input is, by scheme scope id. Omitted, the input is a whole marking.

TestValue.description: Inert JSON data accepted by portable test inputs and expectations.

description: Immutable versioned suite, with complete expectation overrides of inherited cases.

cases.description: The cases this suite adds. Each id must be new to the inheritance chain.

composition.description: Omission inherits the parent; presence replaces the entire composition.

extends.description: The parent suite whose cases this suite inherits, at an exact version.

assertions.description: Replace the inherited case's complete assertion list.

reason.description: Why the inherited expectation is replaced.

overrides.description: Replacement assertions for inherited cases, keyed by case id.

version.description: Exact semantic version of this suite.
